context: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants from the following :
solution:
\(y = 4ax\) ... (1)

Here \(a\) is the arbitrary constant, we differentiate w. r. t. x,

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a\)

then eq. (1) gives

\(y = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) x\) is required differential equation.

context: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants from the following :
solution:
\(y = Ae^{3x} + Be^{-3x}\) ... (1)

Here \(A\) and \(B\) are arbitrary constants.

Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3Ae^{3x} - 3Be^{-3x}\)

again Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 3 \times 3Ae^{3x} - 3 \times 3Be^{-3x}\)

\(= 9\left(Ae^{3x} + Be^{-3x}\right) = 9y\) ... from eq.(1)

\(\therefore \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9y\)

context: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants from the following :
solution:
\(y = (c_1 + c_2 x) e^{x}\) ... (1)

Here \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) are arbitrary constants.

Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = (c_1 + c_2 x) e^{x} + c_2 e^{x}\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + c_2 e^{x}\) ... (2) ... from eq.(1)

Again differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + c_2 e^{x}\)

\(\therefore c_2 e^{x} = \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

put in eq.(2)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\)

context: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants from the following :
solution:
\(y = c^2 + \dfrac{c}{x}\) ... (1)

Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{c}{x^2}\)

\(\therefore c = -x^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

then eq.(1) gives

\(y = \left[-x^2 \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\right]^2 - x^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} \times \dfrac{1}{x}\)

\(\therefore y = x^4 \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - x \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

\(\therefore x^4 \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 0\)

context: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants from the following :
solution:
\(y = c_1 e^{3x} + c_2 e^{2x}\) ... (I)

Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3c_1 e^{3x} + 2c_2 e^{2x}\) ... (II)

Again differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9c_1 e^{3x} + 4c_2 e^{2x}\) ... (III)

As equations (I), (II) and (III) in \(c_1 e^{3x}\) and \(c_2 e^{2x}\) are consistent

\(\therefore \begin{vmatrix} y & 1 & 1 \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} & 3 & 2 \\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} & 9 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 0\)

\(\therefore y(12 - 18) - 1\left(4\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) + 1\left(9\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) = 0\)

\(\therefore -6y - 4\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 9\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\)

\(\therefore -\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 5\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 6y = 0\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 5\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 6y = 0\)

stem: The rate of decay of the mass of a radioactive substance any time is \(k\) times its mass at that time, form the differential equation satisfied by the mass of the substance.
solution:
Let \(m\) be the mass of a radioactive substance at time \('t'\).

\(\therefore\) The rate of decay of mass is \(\dfrac{dm}{dt}\)

Here \(\dfrac{dm}{dt} \propto m\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{dm}{dt} = mk\), where \(k < 0\)

is the required differential equation.

stem: Form the differential equation of family of circles above the X-axis and touching the X-axis at the origin.
solution:
Let \(c(a, b)\) be the centre of the circle touching X-axis at the origin \((b < 0)\).

The radius of the circle is \(b\).

The equation of the circle is

\((x - 0)^2 + (y - b)^2 = b^2\)

\(\therefore x^2 + y^2 - 2by + b^2 = b^2\)

\(\therefore x^2 + y^2 - 2by = 0\) ... (I)

Differentiate w. r. t. x, we get

\(2x + 2y\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) - 2b\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 0\)

\(\therefore x + (y - b)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{x}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)} + (y - b) = 0\)

\(\therefore b = y + \dfrac{x}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}\) ... (II)

From eq. (I) and eq. (II)

\(\therefore x^2 + y^2 - 2\left[y + \dfrac{x}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}\right]y = 0\)

\(\therefore x^2 + y^2 - 2y^2 - \dfrac{2xy}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)} = 0\)

\(\therefore x^2 - y^2 = \dfrac{2xy}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}\)

\(\therefore (x^2 - y^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2xy\)

is the required differential equation.

stem: A particle is moving along the X-axis. Its acceleration at time t is proportional to its velocity at that time. Find the differential equation of the motion of the particle.
solution:
Let \(s\) be the displacement of the particle at time \('t'\).

Its velocity and acceleration are \(\dfrac{ds}{dt}\) and \(\dfrac{d^2s}{dt^2}\) respectively.

Here \(\dfrac{d^2s}{dt^2} \propto \dfrac{ds}{dt}\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{d^2s}{dt^2} = k\dfrac{ds}{dt}\), (where \(k\) is constant \(\neq 0\))

is the required differential equation.
